subject: dm
title: First-order growth
prompt: Solve a_n=(3)*a_(n-1)+(0), n>=1; a_0=2. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: The homogeneous characteristic equation is r-3=0, so a_n=C*3^n.
a_0=2 gives C=2.
Hence a_n=2*3^n.
Check: a_0=2=2. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Two distinct roots
prompt: Solve a_n=(5)*a_(n-1)+(-6)*a_(n-2)+(0), n>=2; a_0=3, a_1=7. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: A+B=3 and 2*A+3*B=7 give A=2, B=1.
Hence a_n=2*2^n+3^n.
Check: a_0=3=3; a_1=7=7. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Distinct roots with negative coefficient
prompt: Solve a_n=(1)*a_(n-1)+(2)*a_(n-2)+(0), n>=2; a_0=2, a_1=1. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: A+B=2 and 2*A-B=1 give A=B=1.
Hence a_n=2^n+(-1)^n.
Check: a_0=2=2; a_1=1=1. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Repeated root two
prompt: Solve a_n=(4)*a_(n-1)+(-4)*a_(n-2)+(0), n>=2; a_0=3, a_1=8. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: a_0=3 gives A=3. a_1=8 gives 2*(3+B)=8, so B=1.
Hence a_n=(3+n)*2^n.
Check: a_0=3=3; a_1=8=8. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Repeated root one
prompt: Solve a_n=(2)*a_(n-1)+(-1)*a_(n-2)+(0), n>=2; a_0=2, a_1=5. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: a_0=2 gives A=2, and a_1=5 gives B=3.
Hence a_n=2+3*n.
Check: a_0=2=2; a_1=5=5. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Alternating repeated root
prompt: Solve a_n=(-2)*a_(n-1)+(-1)*a_(n-2)+(0), n>=2; a_0=1, a_1=-3. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: a_0=1 gives A=1. a_1=-3 gives -(1+B)=-3, so B=2.
Check: a_0=1=1; a_1=-3=-3. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Constant forcing
prompt: Solve a_n=(2)*a_(n-1)+(3), n>=1; a_0=1. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: The homogeneous solution is C*2^n. Try a constant particular solution K.
K=2*K+3 gives K=-3. a_0=1 gives C-3=1, so C=4.
Hence a_n=4*2^n-3.
Check: a_0=1=1. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Resonant constant forcing
prompt: Solve a_n=(1)*a_(n-1)+(4), n>=1; a_0=2. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: The homogeneous solution is C. A constant trial overlaps, so try K*n.
K*n=K*(n-1)+4 gives K=4. a_0=2 gives C=2.
Hence a_n=2+4*n.
Check: a_0=2=2. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Linear forcing
prompt: Solve a_n=(2)*a_(n-1)+(n), n>=1; a_0=0. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: The homogeneous solution is C*2^n. Try A*n+B.
A*n+B=2*(A*(n-1)+B)+n. Coefficient comparison gives A=-1, B=-2.
a_0=0 gives C=2.
Hence a_n=2^(n+1)-n-2.
Check: a_0=0=0. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Exponential forcing distinct
prompt: Solve a_n=(2)*a_(n-1)+(3^n), n>=1; a_0=0. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: The homogeneous solution is C*2^n. Try K*3^n.
a_0=0 gives C=-3.
Hence a_n=3*3^n-3*2^n.
Check: a_0=0=0. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Exponential resonance
prompt: Solve a_n=(2)*a_(n-1)+(2^n), n>=1; a_0=1. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: The root 2 already occurs in the homogeneous solution C*2^n. Try K*n*2^n.
After division by 2^n: K*n=K*(n-1)+1, so K=1.
a_0=1 gives C=1.
Hence a_n=(1+n)*2^n.
Check: a_0=1=1. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Second-order constant forcing
prompt: Solve a_n=(3)*a_(n-1)+(-2)*a_(n-2)+(1), n>=2; a_0=0, a_1=0. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: The roots of r^2-3*r+2=0 are 1 and 2. The homogeneous solution is A+B*2^n.
A constant trial overlaps root 1, so try C*n. Substitution gives C*n=C*n+C+1, so C=-1.
a_0=0 gives A+B=0. a_1=0 gives A+2*B-1=0. Thus B=1, A=-1.
Hence a_n=2^n-n-1.
Check: a_0=0=0; a_1=0=0. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Repeated resonance with constant
prompt: Solve a_n=(2)*a_(n-1)+(-1)*a_(n-2)+(2), n>=2; a_0=0, a_1=1. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: The characteristic polynomial is (r-1)^2. Homogeneous solution is A+B*n.
A constant forcing overlaps a root of multiplicity 2, so try C*n^2. Its second difference is 2*C; hence C=1.
a_0=0 gives A=0. a_1=1 gives B=0.
Hence a_n=n^2.
Check: a_0=0=0; a_1=1=1. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Quadratic forcing accumulation
prompt: Solve a_n=(1)*a_(n-1)+(n^2), n>=1; a_0=0. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: Iterate a_n=a_(n-1)+n^2 to obtain a_n=a_0+sum_(i=1)^n i^2.
Since a_0=0, use sum of squares to get n*(n+1)*(2*n+1)/6.
Check: a_0=0=0. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Two roots with exponential forcing
prompt: Solve a_n=(5)*a_(n-1)+(-6)*a_(n-2)+(4^n), n>=2; a_0=1, a_1=4. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: The homogeneous solution is A*2^n+B*3^n. Try C*4^n.
Substitution gives C*(16-20+6)=16, so C=8.
a_0=1 gives A+B=-7. a_1=4 gives 2*A+3*B=-28. Thus B=-14, A=7.
Check: a_0=1=1; a_1=4=4. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Resonance at a repeated root
prompt: Solve a_n=(4)*a_(n-1)+(-4)*a_(n-2)+(2^n), n>=2; a_0=0, a_1=2. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: The homogeneous solution is (A+B*n)*2^n. Divide by 2^n and put b_n=a_n/2^n.
Therefore a_n=n*(n+1)*2^(n-1).
Hence a_n=n*(n+1)*2^(n-1).
Check: a_0=0=0; a_1=2=2. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

title: Iteration with constant decrement
prompt: Solve a_n=(1)*a_(n-1)+(-3), n>=1; a_0=10. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: Iterating gives a_n=a_(n-1)-3=a_(n-2)-6=...=a_0-3*n.
Hence a_n=10-3*n.
Check: a_0=10=10. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Third-order roots
prompt: Solve a_n=(6)*a_(n-1)+(-11)*a_(n-2)+(6)*a_(n-3)+(0), n>=3; a_0=3, a_1=6, a_2=14. Show the method and check initial conditions.

solution.text: The form is A+B*2^n+C*3^n. Initial values give A+B+C=3, A+2*B+3*C=6, A+4*B+9*C=14.
Subtract equations: B+2*C=3 and 2*B+6*C=8, so C=1,B=1,A=1.
Hence a_n=1+2^n+3^n.
Check: a_0=3=3; a_1=6=6; a_2=14=14. Substitution into the recurrence gives the stated forcing term.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

title: Repeated-root trial
prompt: The characteristic polynomial is (r-2)^2 and the forcing is 2^n. Which particular trial is appropriate?

solution.text: The unadjusted trial C*2^n overlaps the root 2.
Root 2 has multiplicity 2, so multiply by n^2.
Use a_n(particular)=C*n^2*2^n, then substitute to solve C.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.

subject: dm
title: Roots two and four

solution.text: Characteristic equation: r^2-6*r+8=(r-2)*(r-4)=0.
Thus a_n=A*2^n+B*4^n.
Initial conditions give A+B=4 and 2*A+4*B=10. Subtract twice the first equation: 2*B=2, so B=1 and A=3.
Hence a_n=3*2^n+4^n. Check a_0=4 and a_1=10.

conceptNote: Use characteristic roots for the homogeneous part, adjust particular trials for resonance, and apply initial conditions to the whole solution.
